asset.title: Analytics without cookies or fingerprinting data
asset.content:
Subject: Analytics without cookies or fingerprinting data
Preview text: Review the open-source browser script and its documented collection boundaries.

See what runs in the visitor’s browser

Hi there,

Simple Analytics publishes its browser-facing analytics scripts as open source on GitHub. Municipal web and privacy teams can inspect what runs in a visitor’s browser before deciding whether a formal evaluation is warranted.

Simple Analytics is privacy-focused website analytics software. It measures website activity without collecting personal data, using cookies or gathering information that could fingerprint a visitor, so its own analytics script does not depend on visitor consent.

The documentation links directly to the user-facing source code and explains configurable script behaviour, including which pages, metrics and parameters can be collected or ignored. That gives technical and privacy reviewers a concrete basis for assessment.

The linked page lets your team examine the code and configuration options before deciding whether Simple Analytics should advance to a formal evaluation alongside the municipality’s current analytics setup.

Inspect the user-facing scripts → https://docs.simpleanalytics.com/script

- Simple Analytics

asset_metadata.single_idea: Before adding another analytics script to a municipal website, the team can inspect Simple Analytics' open-source user-facing scripts and assess a documented design that avoids personal data, cookies and fingerprinting information.

selected_brief.selection_reason: A public-sector team may need an inspectable technical basis before it is willing to discuss deployment; the published user-facing scripts provide a smaller, read-only first step.

value_case.reader_benefit: The municipality can consider analytics that avoids collecting personal data, using cookies or gathering fingerprinting information, while giving technical and privacy reviewers access to inspect the user-facing scripts.
value_case.mechanism: Simple Analytics states that it collects no personal data, uses no cookies and gathers no information that could fingerprint a user; its user-facing scripts are open source on GitHub.
decision_conditions: Reviewing published scripts does not establish procurement approval, a data processing agreement, SOC 2 status or suitability for the municipality's complete technology stack.

claim_conditions: Keep the argument within Dutch municipalities.
Describe the benefit as visibility into traffic sources and browsing behavior, not individual-level tracking.
Present the 30-day proof of concept as a comparison and reporting-fit evaluation alongside GA4, with GA4 and the consent banner left in place.
Add the documented script tag at the end of the <body>, optionally with the noscript image fallback (E38).
Use a published platform guide where the site runs on Squarespace, Webflow, Wix or Google Tag Manager (E29).
Point a own-subdomain custom domain at the documented external host via DNS if ad-blocker bypass is wanted (fact_2072cb5cdcb9e581, fact_28a266c91bbbc122).
Add the exact hostname in the dashboard for shared preview/proxy domains, whose data is otherwise dropped (E43).
Leave the AI assistant un-opted-in to keep data inside the EU (E79).

Every required capability in the audience definition is covered by selected evidence, but the dossier establishes no data processing agreement and SOC 2 is only 'in progress' (E106), data leaves the EU if the AI assistant is opted into (E79), shared preview/proxy hostnames are dropped unless added (E43), and the researched municipal situation rests on sources dated 2019-2020 or undated, so present applicability is not corroborated.

The problem as researched covers Google Analytics, Google Fonts and YouTube loading before consent; the selected evidence only covers replacing the analytics component, and nothing here addresses Fonts or embedded YouTube.
Frame script inspection as an input to review, not proof of legal approval or security certification.
